say: Nikita, I’ll ask coworking contacts for introductions to two small hotels, not promise participants. Let’s select arrival routes first so we test coverage, not cherry-picked questions.
Mārtiņš, agreed. I’ll check restrictions separately; let’s also time couriers finding a relevant restriction versus their usual source. Faster with no extra errors, or we rethink.
Mārtiņš, thanks, checking has owners now. I’m keeping my card until couriers return; I’ll alternate test order so our briefing doesn’t win just because they’ve already seen the question.
I oppose I38 because recurring safe missions remain unproven. I budget €3.50 for coffee; what makes I42 worth seven coffees monthly to a hotel?
I38 “Pond Patrol” is dropped: voted down (8 oppose, 1 back).
Nikita, €25 is two tutoring hours at €12.50 for me. How many reception minutes must I42 save monthly to justify that price?
I back I36’s free pilot. Checking has owners, and comparison with couriers’ usual sources can show whether it saves time rather than adds reading.

On our Kaunas export team, paperwork matters because an order depends on it, not because someone opens it. I’m still withholding I36 support until couriers return and identify a restriction that helped their shift.
